info.title: Lead OS API
info.summary: The API the product itself uses, reachable with an API key.
info.description:
Every answer carries the same envelope: `{ success, data, meta }` on success and
`{ success: false, error: { code, message, details?, requestId } }` on a refusal.

Two credentials reach this API. A session token, which the web app uses, and an API key:
`Authorization: Bearer <key id>.<secret>`. A key may only do what the member who created
it can do, narrowed to the scopes it was given — so the permission named on each endpoint
has to be in the key’s scopes **and** held by that member.

Errors are listed with their meaning and what to do about them at `/docs/errors`.

data.description: The endpoint’s payload. A list endpoint answers an array.

message.description: Written for a person. Show it rather than paraphrasing it — a refusal we worded is the one thing not to replace with "that is not allowed".

details.description: Field errors on a 400, or context on a refusal.

Error400.description:
`INVALID_CUSTOM_FIELD` — A custom field’s value did not match its definition — the type, or its options.

`INVALID_PHONE` — A phone number could not be read as a number in the workspace’s country.

`UNKNOWN_FIELD` — A field was sent that this endpoint does not accept.

`VALIDATION_FAILED` — The request body or query did not match the endpoint’s schema.

Error401.description:
`INVALID_API_KEY` — The key is unknown, revoked, expired, belongs to another workspace, or its secret does not match. One answer for all of them, deliberately.

`TOKEN_EXPIRED` — The access token is past its lifetime.

`TOKEN_REUSED` — A refresh token was presented twice, which means it may have been stolen, so the whole session family was revoked.

`UNAUTHENTICATED` — No credential was presented, or the access token has expired.

Error403.description:
`FEATURE_NOT_IN_PLAN` — The endpoint belongs to a feature the workspace’s plan does not include.

`FORBIDDEN` — The caller is known but may not do this — an address off a key’s allowlist, or a route that is only for a signed-in person.

`LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — A plan quota is full — seats, leads, messages. A business condition, which is why it is not a 429.

`ORG_SUSPENDED` — The workspace is suspended or cancelled, so it accepts no writes.

`OUT_OF_DATA_SCOPE` — The permission is held, but not widely enough: the route needs it across the branch or the organization.

`PERMISSION_DENIED` — The permission this route declares is not held.

`SUBSCRIPTION_INACTIVE` — The subscription is past due or cancelled.

`TRIAL_EXPIRED` — The trial has ended, so the workspace is in read-only mode.

Error404.description: `NOT_FOUND` — No such resource — or it belongs to another workspace, or a malformed id was sent. Indistinguishable on purpose.

Error409.description:
`CONFLICT` — The write conflicts with what is already stored, usually a uniqueness rule.

`DUPLICATE_LEAD` — The workspace’s duplicate rules matched an existing lead.

`IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY_MISMATCH` — An `Idempotency-Key` was reused with a different body.

`STALE_VERSION` — Somebody changed the record since the version that was sent.

Error422.description: `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION` — The request is well-formed and the product refuses it — a quotation already sent, a counter that cannot move backwards.

Error429.description: `RATE_LIMITED` — Too many requests in the window — a technical condition, unlike `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

Error500.description: `INTERNAL_ERROR` — Our fault. The response carries a `requestId`.

sessionToken.description: A signed-in person’s access token, from `POST /auth/login`.

apiKey.description: An API key, as `<key id>.<secret>` — the two halves shown once when the key is created.
